title: Cave carving: the network, or the room
question: Which one reads as a cave system you would want to walk into? You said of round 5 that it 'looks like a single room instead of a cave system' — does either of these still do that?
context_md:
Same seed (3, canyon), same camera, same crop — only the cave-carving
constants differ. Both have a shaft mined down from the surface so the
chamber can be photographed at all.

I have already ruled against one of these on measurement and told the
implementation agent to revert it, so this is posted blind as a check on
me rather than as an open question. If your eye disagrees with the
numbers, the numbers lose.

What the corrected census says over 16 seeds x 5 presets:

|                       | one | other |
|---|---|---|
| span across (cells)   | 136 | 70    |
| tallest open column   | 41  | 63    |
| chamber/passage contrast | 5.4x | 2.1x |
| walkable regions      | 1   | 1     |
| of the void he can walk | 33-37% | 96% |

Background you should have, because it reverses something I told you
earlier: the "round-5 caves are 0% reachable, you cannot enter them at
any point" finding was **wrong**. The probe that produced it counted
stalactites and stalagmites as walls — but since the scenery change they
are walk-through, so it was measuring the decoration, not the passage.
Corrected, round 5's caves are one connected walkable region you can
traverse end to end. What made them read as unenterable was the picket
fence of one-pixel formations filling the view, which is being rebuilt
now as fewer and thicker.

Formations in both shots are still round 5's one-pixel ones; that work is
in flight and is not what this card is about.
